name: Natural History Museum of Utah
unique: A copper clad building above the valley with a dinosaur wall of 60 skeletons, a Great Salt Lake exhibit and a gallery on the Fremont and Ancestral Puebloan cultures.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the native voices gallery are the two reasons to come; the building's design and the terrace view of the Wasatch are the bonus.

name: Red Butte Garden
unique: A hundred acres in the foothills with a water conservation garden, a children's garden and a summer concert series in the amphitheater.
buzz: The water wise garden is the local lesson and the concerts sell out; the upper trails are steep and the view over the city is the rest.

name: Snowbird
unique: A steep resort at the top of Little Cottonwood Canyon with a tram to 11,000 feet, 500 inches of snow in a good year and a summer ride to a ridge walk.
buzz: Skiers say the terrain is as serious as anywhere in the country and the canyon closes for avalanches; the tram runs year round.

name: Bridal Veil Falls
unique: A 607 foot double cataract at the mouth of Provo Canyon, with a paved trail to the base and a pool that freezes into a blue cone in winter.
buzz: The walk is short and paved and the falls are visible from the road; the ice climb in winter is a local spectacle.

name: Museum of Ancient Life
unique: One of the largest dinosaur museums in the world, with 60 mounted skeletons, a working paleontology lab and a walk through the eras of life.
buzz: Children who are serious about dinosaurs will want three hours; the lab where fossils are prepared is the part adults linger at.

name: Timpanogos Cave
unique: Three connected caves full of helicitites and anthodites at the end of a steep 1.5 mile trail, with a view down the canyon the whole way.
buzz: The hike is the hard part and the cave tour is the reward; tickets sell out and the trail is hot and exposed.

name: Cedar Breaks
unique: A natural amphitheater at 10,000 feet with hoodoos in pink and orange limestone, less visited than Bryce and just as strange.
buzz: The rim trail at sunset is the photograph and the altitude is real; the road closes with snow from November to May.

name: Brian Head
unique: The highest base elevation of any resort in the state, with a long beginner run and red rock views from the lifts.
buzz: Families like the price and the lack of crowds; the terrain is modest and the drive from Las Vegas is four hours.

name: Parowan Gap
customer: Rock art people, road trippers, photographers
unique: A wind cut gap in the rock covered with hundreds of petroglyphs, including a calendar spiral that marks the solstice.
buzz: Archaeologists argue about the meanings and the site is free and unguarded; the drive is a short detour off Interstate 15.

name: The Wave
unique: A sandstone formation of red and pink swirls in Coyote Buttes North, reachable only by a six mile round trip hike and a permit that thousands apply for daily.
buzz: The lottery is the hard part and the navigation is the second; people who get in describe it as the best rock in the southwest.

name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes
unique: Pink sand dunes between red cliffs where a slot canyon funnels wind into ripples, with an ATV riding area and a closed preserve for a rare beetle.
buzz: Sandboarding down the big dune is the family fun and the ATV rental is at the entrance; the sand is hot in summer and the wind is constant.

name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
unique: The largest no kill animal sanctuary in the country, in Angel Canyon, with tours of the dog, cat and horse areas and volunteer shifts you can book.
buzz: Visitors say the tour is moving and the canyon setting is beautiful; you cannot adopt on a whim but you can walk dogs for a morning.

name: Valley of the Gods
unique: A 17 mile dirt road through red monoliths and mesas that look like Monument Valley without the fees or the crowds.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the camping is free; the road is graded but rough after rain and there are no services.

name: Natural Bridges National Monument
unique: Three natural stone bridges in a canyon with a loop road and trails underneath, plus a dark sky designation and Ancestral Puebloan ruins on the mesa.
buzz: The Owachomo bridge at sunset is the photograph and the canyon hike is quiet; the park is remote and the nearest town is 40 minutes away.

name: Goosenecks
unique: The San Juan River loops through a 1,000 foot deep meander three times in a mile, one of the most dramatic incised meanders in the world.
buzz: The overlook is a short walk and the scale is hard to photograph; it is a 15 minute stop that people remember longer than expected.

name: Heber Valley Railroad
unique: A heritage railroad along Deer Creek Reservoir into Provo Canyon, with a steam engine on some weekends and a murder mystery train at night.
buzz: The canyon view from the open car is the reason to ride; the themed trains sell out and the ride is 90 minutes.

name: Wasatch Mountain State Park
unique: Twenty three thousand acres in the Wasatch foothills with a golf course, a reservoir and trails that climb into aspen, 20 minutes from Park City.
buzz: Locals use it for camping and fall color and the golf is cheap; the trails are shared with bikes and horses.

name: Dinosaur National Monument
unique: A quarry wall with 1,500 dinosaur bones still embedded in the rock, inside a building built over the dig, plus canyons where the Green and Yampa rivers meet.
buzz: The quarry wall is the thing people come for and it is better than any mounted skeleton; the river rafting through the canyon is the local secret.

name: Utah Field House of Natural History
unique: A museum with a garden of full size dinosaur sculptures, a walk through time hall and a fossil prep lab, next to the road into the monument.
buzz: The outdoor dinosaur garden is the photograph and the inside is a good rainy day stop; it takes 90 minutes.

name: Red Fleet State Park
unique: A reservoir with a dinosaur trackway on the shore and a hike to tracks left by a three toed dinosaur 200 million years ago.
buzz: The trackway hike is the reason to come and the water is warm enough to swim in summer; the reservoir levels drop late in the season.

name: Canyonlands: Island in the Sky
unique: A mesa between the Green and Colorado rivers with overlooks into a canyon system the size of a small state, including Mesa Arch at sunrise.
buzz: Mesa Arch is the photograph and the Grand View Point trail is the walk; the park is 40 minutes from Moab and far emptier than Arches.

name: Dead Horse Point
unique: A promontory 2,000 feet above a gooseneck of the Colorado with a view into Canyonlands, where cowboys once corralled wild horses on a neck of land.
buzz: Sunrise from the point is the classic and the mountain bike trail along the rim is a classic ride; the park is quieter than the national parks.

name: Colorado River Rafting from Moab
unique: A float through the red rock canyon below Moab with Class II and III rapids, a beach lunch and a view of arches and petroglyphs from the water.
buzz: The full day Fisher Towers section is the standard and the water is warm in summer; book ahead for holidays and bring sunscreen.

name: Snow Canyon
unique: Red and white sandstone formations with lava tubes, petrified sand dunes and a slot canyon, 15 minutes from St. George and often overlooked for Zion.
buzz: The Petrified Dunes trail and the lava tube are the local favorites; summer heat is brutal and the park is best at sunrise.

name: Tuacahn Amphitheatre
unique: A outdoor amphitheater in a red rock canyon where Broadway musicals use the cliff as a backdrop and mist the stage in summer heat.
buzz: The setting is the reason people go and the productions are better than expected; bring a cushion and expect a long walk from parking.

name: Utah Olympic Park
unique: The ski jumping and bobsled venue from the 2002 Games, with a museum, a zip line and a summer bobsled ride down the track.
buzz: The bobsled ride is the thrill and the ski jump elevator is the view; the museum is small but the athletes training are real.

name: High West Distillery
unique: A distillery on a historic ranch with a saloon and a barrel room, making rye whiskey at altitude in a state that used to ban the stuff.
buzz: The tasting is generous and the food is better than a distillery needs; the original Park City location is smaller and harder to park at.

name: Lagoon Amusement Park
unique: A 1886 resort with a wooden coaster, a pioneer village of moved buildings and a lagoon, still family owned and still a Utah summer ritual.
buzz: The wooden coaster and the pioneer village are the reasons locals defend it; the park is dated in places and the water park costs extra.

name: Great Salt Lake Shorelands Preserve
unique: A boardwalk through wetland and upland where the Great Salt Lake's brine flies and shrimp feed millions of migrating birds, with a visitor center and tower.
buzz: Birders come in spring and fall and the boardwalk is flat; the lake levels have dropped and the shoreline has moved.

name: Topaz Museum
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: A museum in Delta telling the story of the 11,000 Japanese Americans imprisoned at Topaz during the war, with barracks, artifacts and an art school that flourished behind barbed wire.
buzz: Visitors say it is one of the most important small museums in the country; the site itself is 16 miles out of town and marked by a monument.
